nodes.label: CLAUDE.md — Repo Guidance
nodes.rationale: Planning-complete, pre-code repo; spec wins over design docs; D1-D14 not to be re-litigated without the owner.

nodes.label: vector-syncer System
nodes.rationale: Automates export-convert-embed: mirrors one OneDrive folder tree into Qdrant (one collection per top-level subfolder) so documents become searchable by any RAG app; OneDrive stays the single source of truth.

nodes.label: Worker (Node.js/TypeScript Orchestrator)
nodes.rationale: Node owns everything stateful and scheduled (auth, delta walking, jobs, chunking, embedding calls, sparse encoding, Qdrant writes) because BullMQ is Node-first; it never parses document formats.

nodes.label: Converter Service (Python FastAPI Sidecar)
nodes.rationale: Stateless bytes-to-Markdown sidecar (POST /convert): keeps Python deps out of the Node image, keeps MarkItDown imports warm, isolates conversion crashes/OOM, scales independently (D3).

nodes.label: Redis
nodes.rationale: Holds BullMQ queues and sync state; hard requirements: maxmemory-policy noeviction (BullMQ corrupts under eviction) + AOF; fully rebuildable, never long-term truth.

nodes.label: Qdrant
nodes.rationale: Vector DB holding one collection per base folder plus od_catalog — the product of the whole pipeline; user requirement (payload filtering, indexes, aliases for zero-downtime reindex).

nodes.label: BullMQ
nodes.rationale: Provides Job Schedulers (cron), retries/backoff, manual rate limiting, deduplication, live concurrency — all built in; multi-process scale-out is a deploy change, not a code change.

nodes.label: MarkItDown
nodes.rationale: Microsoft's Python-only converter (PDF/DOCX/PPTX/XLSX/EPUB/MSG/images/ZIP to Markdown); its breadth and OCR integrations would take weeks to approximate in Node — the reason Python exists in the stack.

nodes.label: DeepInfra (AI Provider)
nodes.rationale: Single OpenAI-compatible provider for all three models — one key, one dashboard; a config value (OPENAI_BASE_URL), not a dependency: any OpenAI-compatible provider slots in without code changes (D11).

nodes.label: OpenAI SDK
nodes.rationale: The only AI client allowed in code; its native OPENAI_BASE_URL/OPENAI_API_KEY env vars keep provider, endpoint and model IDs pure configuration.

nodes.label: BAAI/bge-m3 Embedding Model
nodes.rationale: 1024-d dense, 8k-token input, 100+ languages, cheap; the OpenAI-compatible endpoint returns dense only; swapping it changes dimensions and forces a full re-index — finalize before the first backfill.

nodes.label: Qwen3-VL OCR Model
nodes.rationale: Qwen/Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B-Instruct vision-LLM reads images embedded in PDF/DOCX/PPTX/XLSX (scans, screenshots, diagrams) via the markitdown-ocr plugin; swappable anytime with zero migration.

nodes.label: DeepSeek-V4-Flash LLM
nodes.rationale: Generates catalog collection descriptions; available for future summarization needs.

nodes.label: Azure Document Intelligence (Fallback OCR)
nodes.rationale: Full layout OCR via docintel_endpoint; kept as fallback tier if Qwen3-VL underperforms on complex layouts.

nodes.label: MSAL Node
nodes.rationale: @azure/msal-node: acquireTokenByDeviceCode for bootstrap, acquireTokenSilent at runtime, pluggable ICachePlugin for the encrypted persistent cache.

nodes.label: Entra App Registration
nodes.rationale: Public client (no secret, no redirect URI, public client flows enabled) — possession of the encrypted token cache is the effective credential; least-privilege delegated scopes Files.Read + offline_access + User.Read.

nodes.label: sync Queue
nodes.rationale: Concurrency 1 is a correctness invariant, not a tuning knob: delta walks must never overlap; manual triggers simply queue behind a running walk.

nodes.label: files Queue
nodes.rationale: Fan-out: process-file, delete-file/folder, update-metadata, refresh-catalog; deduplicated, independently rate-limited and retried; concurrency N default 4, live-adjustable.

nodes.label: BullMQ Job Scheduler
nodes.rationale: upsertJobScheduler is idempotent by scheduler ID — safe on every startup; drives delta-sync cron (default */5) and weekly reconcile.

nodes.label: /health Endpoint
nodes.rationale: Reports auth state, last sync, queue depths, effective concurrency, and counters (empty_conversion, ocr_images_processed) — OCR spend is observable before the invoice.

nodes.label: od_catalog Catalog Collection
nodes.rationale: One embedded, LLM-described point per document collection so consumers (especially agents) can enumerate deterministically (scroll) and semantically route queries (vector search) before searching (D13); also the tool-shape for a future MCP server.

nodes.label: Conversation Store (app_conversations)
nodes.rationale: Consumer-owned collection outside od_*; the worker's namespace boundary (only od_* + od_catalog are ever touched) guarantees it can never be collateral damage; a conversationId alone retrieves the ordered transcript.

nodes.label: Shared Consumer Package
nodes.rationale: Consumer app imports the exact bm25-v1 module and conversation-store helpers instead of reimplementing — prevents tokenizer/hash drift that would silently degrade hybrid recall; built in Phase 4; the worker never calls the helpers.

nodes.label: docker-compose Stack
nodes.rationale: Whole stack (redis, qdrant, converter, worker) reproducible on any Linux host; everything loopback-only; deployment is Docker on WSL2 now, VPS later = copy .env + data/ + volumes (Q5).

nodes.label: Environment Variable Configuration
nodes.rationale: All config via zod-validated env vars, fail-fast at startup; the three model IDs are initial preferences, not commitments; secrets only in .env (0600, gitignored).

nodes.label: Operations Runbook
nodes.rationale: Procedures for first-time setup, re-auth, manual sync, full resync, rebuilds, catalog refresh, pause/resume, live concurrency, backups — validated once each in Phase 5.

nodes.label: Redis Sync State (vs:* keys)
nodes.rationale: deltaLink, root ids, base-folder-to-collection map, folder map, per-file cTag/hash/chunk-count/status; every key documents what losing it costs — all rebuildable from OneDrive + Qdrant payloads (D5: no SQL database).

nodes.label: Graph Delta Query
nodes.rationale: Returns only items changed since the stored deltaLink, recursively over the whole subtree; the first run doubles as initial indexing; exact $select list pins the fields; polling chosen over webhooks for v1 (D9).

nodes.label: Delta Item Classification
nodes.rationale: Maps each delta item (deleted/folder/file facets, cTag comparison, base-folder resolution via the vs:folder map) to the right job: process, re-route, metadata patch, delete, or skip; edge cases parked for the Phase-1 spike.

nodes.label: 410 Gone Resync
nodes.rationale: Expired delta token: follow the Location header to a fresh enumeration, classify normally (hash-skip keeps it cheap), reconcile deletions, store the new token — the same code path as manual full resync: one implementation, two triggers.

nodes.label: Delegated Auth (Silent Refresh)
nodes.rationale: Hard user constraint: act as the signed-in user, never app-only/admin consent; interactive once then silent forever; interaction_required is a first-class alert state (health flips, runbook message) — never a crash loop.

nodes.label: Device Code Flow Bootstrap
nodes.rationale: One-time yarn auth CLI prints URL + code; simpler headless than an auth-code/PKCE redirect listener (D2).

nodes.label: Encrypted MSAL Token Cache
nodes.rationale: Custom ~40-line ICachePlugin (AES-256-GCM with MSAL_CACHE_KEY, random IV, atomic tmp+rename write, 0600) because msal-node-extensions targets desktop keychains, not headless containers; lives on a volume so re-auth survives rebuilds.

nodes.label: Change-Notification Webhooks (v2)
nodes.rationale: Deferred: needs a public HTTPS notificationUrl and still requires delta calls (notifications carry no item details) — a latency win only; a notification would just trigger the existing sync job early.

nodes.label: cTag Change Detection
nodes.rationale: cTag changes only when content changes (eTag also churns on metadata); preference order: quickXorHash/sha256 content hashes, then cTag as an opaque equality token.

nodes.label: OCR Strategy Tiers
nodes.rationale: Chosen: Qwen3-VL vision OCR inline, on by default, no budget machinery — the corpus is mostly digital PDFs with minimal images (D8); tiers: off (OCR_LLM_MODEL empty = kill switch), Azure DocIntel fallback, local Tesseract offline; documented add-backs if reality disagrees: per-cycle image cap, targeted re-process status.

nodes.label: Empty-Conversion Warning
nodes.rationale: PDF/image yielding under ~200 chars/page: index nothing, log a warning, increment the /health counter — a warning light, not a workflow; bulk redo is resync --rebuild.

nodes.label: Heading-Aware Chunking
nodes.rationale: 512-token target, 64 overlap, min 20; heading-breadcrumb prefix goes only on the embedding input (payload keeps raw text and heading_path separate); tables/code kept intact, split tables repeat headers; js-tiktoken is a plus/minus 20% proxy for bge-m3's tokenizer — irrelevant far below the 8192 ceiling.

nodes.label: Collection per Base Folder
nodes.rationale: Each top-level subfolder isolates into od_{slug} (alias over versioned physical, created lazily, dropped with the folder); mapping keyed by folder ID so renames don't break; accepted costs (D12): global search = client-side fan-out, per-collection HNSW overhead — revisit past a few dozen folders.

nodes.label: Deterministic UUIDv5 Point IDs
nodes.rationale: uuidv5(driveId/itemId#chunkIndex, fixed namespace): re-processing computes identical IDs so upserts overwrite and retries are free; collection-independent, so cross-collection moves are plain delete+insert.

nodes.label: Point Payload Schema
nodes.rationale: Every point self-describing and attributable without a second lookup (FR-14): file identity, path, authorship, timestamps, heading path, raw chunk text, content hash, embed_model and sparse_encoder version guards; indexed fields (file_id, ancestor_ids, extension, mime_type, last_modified_ts) power deletes and filters.

nodes.label: bm25-v1 Sparse Encoder
nodes.rationale: ~100 lines worker-local, no API call: unicode tokenize, FNV-1a hash to u32 indices, BM25 TF saturation (k1=1.2, b=0.75, avgLen=256); IDF stays server-side via modifier:idf so it tracks the live corpus; shared code with the consumer app — version bump = cheap sparse-only backfill, golden-vector tests pin the encoding.

nodes.label: Delete-Then-Upsert per File
nodes.rationale: Delete by file_id filter then upsert the new set (wait:true) guarantees no stale chunks survive shrinkage; the milliseconds-long zero-point window is accepted (D7) over more complex trailing-delete schemes.

nodes.label: Hybrid RRF Search
nodes.rationale: Every point carries dense + sparse from day one (D14): exact tokens (codes, invoice numbers) hit via the sparse side, paraphrases via dense; queries prefetch both slots and fuse with RRF; query embedding must match the indexing model, query sparse must use the identical bm25-v1 module.

nodes.label: Alias-Flip Rebuild
nodes.rationale: Physical collections are versioned (_vN) behind stable aliases: rebuild into _v2, flip the alias, drop _v1 — zero-downtime re-index for embedding-model or chunking changes; Qdrant's additive createVectorName migration is the alternative path.

nodes.label: Weekly Reconcile
nodes.rationale: Safety net for delta edge cases and stragglers: full enumeration fixes stale paths, orphaned file_ids, hash mismatches, catalog stats/descriptions, orphaned collections; cheap because hash-skip makes untouched files no-ops.

nodes.label: Job Deduplication (itemId:cTag)
nodes.rationale: Same content version queued once: re-walking an uncommitted delta window collapses silently; a newer cTag is a new dedup ID and the older job completes as superseded after its metadata re-fetch.

nodes.label: Manual Rate Limiting (429 Handling)
nodes.rationale: worker.rateLimit(retryAfter) + Worker.RateLimitError pauses the whole queue without consuming a retry attempt — honors Retry-After from both Graph and DeepInfra; static limiter (max 8 jobs/sec) as safety net.

nodes.label: Runtime-Adjustable Files Concurrency
nodes.rationale: worker.concurrency is a public setter: cli.js concurrency <n> writes a Redis config key, applied live with no restart, reported on /health; the sync worker is deliberately not adjustable — its concurrency 1 is a correctness invariant.

nodes.label: Retry Matrix
nodes.rationale: 429s never consume attempts; transient errors backoff exponentially x4; bad files complete as skipped_* statuses (not errors); auth interaction_required is UnrecoverableError plus red health.

nodes.label: OneDrive as Source of Truth
nodes.rationale: Qdrant and Redis are derived, rebuildable indexes; losing the delta token costs a re-enumeration (hash-skip avoids re-embedding), never data — the principle behind every recovery path.

nodes.label: Idempotency Principle
nodes.rationale: NFR-1: every job safe to run twice, at-least-once delivery end to end — achieved via deterministic point IDs, dedup IDs, delete-then-upsert, and content-hash skips.

nodes.label: At-Least-Once Delivery
nodes.rationale: Delta token advances only after the full page walk and all enqueues (D6); a crash mid-walk re-reads the same window and dedup collapses duplicates; a poison file fails visibly in Bull Board without wedging the token.

nodes.label: Hybrid Node + Python Runtime
nodes.rationale: The two anchor requirements pull apart: BullMQ is Node-native, MarkItDown is Python-only; all-TS rejected (no MarkItDown equivalent), all-Python rejected (BullMQ py client trails on Job Schedulers/rateLimit); the seam is one HTTP endpoint — also the crash-isolation boundary (D1).

nodes.label: Implementation Phases P0-P6
nodes.rationale: P0 bootstrap, P1 auth+graph spike, P2 queues, P3 conversion, P4 indexing (= MVP), P5 hardening, P6 extensions backlog; each phase has acceptance criteria; later plans are written only at phase boundaries because spike findings feed them.

nodes.label: MVP (End of Phase 4)
nodes.rationale: Acceptance = requirements doc section 7: add/edit/delete round-trips, kill-mid-sync safety, base-folder routing and moves, hybrid RRF plus exact-token recall, complete catalog enumeration.

nodes.label: Phase-1 Graph Spike
nodes.rationale: Verifies empirically what docs cannot promise: folder-scoped delta behavior on the real drive type, which file.hashes exist, what move-out-of-scope and folder-rename emit — findings encoded as regression tests and doc updates in 04 section 4.

nodes.label: D1: Hybrid Runtime
nodes.rationale: Node/TS orchestrator + Python conversion sidecar; all-Python rejected (BullMQ py client trails the Node reference), all-Node rejected (no MarkItDown equivalent).

nodes.label: D2: Delegated Auth via Device Code
nodes.rationale: User constraint; device code is simpler headless than a PKCE redirect listener; app-only client credentials would violate the delegated requirement.
nodes.norm_label: d2: delegated auth via device code

nodes.label: D3: Conversion as HTTP Sidecar
nodes.rationale: Warm imports, crash isolation, clean images; markitdown as CLI child-process kept as the documented minimal-mode fallback if the stack must shrink.

nodes.label: D4: bge-m3 via DeepInfra
nodes.rationale: Model ID is an initial preference, env-swappable — but an embedding swap means re-index, so finalize before the first big backfill; self-hosted FlagEmbedding sidecar (same model, dense and sparse, zero egress) is the documented switch-back path.

nodes.label: D5: Sync State in Redis
nodes.rationale: No SQL database: state is fully rebuildable from OneDrive + Qdrant payloads; revisit only if audit history is ever required.

nodes.label: D6: Advance Delta Token After Enqueue
nodes.rationale: Not after all jobs complete — FlowProducer parent-child gating rejected because a single poison file would wedge the token forever; at-least-once + dedup + reconcile instead of exactly-once illusions.
nodes.norm_label: d6: advance delta token after enqueue

nodes.label: D7: Delete-by-Filter Then Upsert
nodes.rationale: Simpler than upsert plus trailing delete of chunk_index >= n; the brief zero-point window is unnoticeable at this scale.

nodes.label: D8: LLM-Vision OCR, Inline, No Budget Machinery
nodes.rationale: Qwen3-VL on by default because the corpus is image-light (user 2026-07-26); budget guard and --no-ocr staged backfill dropped as over-engineering; cap + targeted re-process are documented add-backs; DocIntel and Tesseract kept as fallbacks.
nodes.norm_label: d8: llm-vision ocr, inline, no budget machinery

nodes.label: D9: Polling Delta, Webhooks Deferred
nodes.rationale: Webhooks need a public HTTPS endpoint and still require delta calls — a latency win only.

nodes.label: D10: Self-Hosted Qdrant in Compose
nodes.rationale: Versioned collections + aliases; Qdrant Cloud fine too — only QDRANT_URL/API_KEY change.

nodes.label: D11: One AI Provider (DeepInfra via OpenAI SDK)
nodes.rationale: One key/dashboard beats best-of-breed sprawl and full self-hosting ops burden; flexibility clause: only the official OpenAI SDK, endpoint + key in its native env vars, every model ID env config — DeepInfra is a value, not a dependency; accepted consequence: document content is processed by the configured provider.
nodes.norm_label: d11: one ai provider (deepinfra via openai sdk)

nodes.label: D12: One Collection per Base Folder
nodes.rationale: Created on demand, loose root files to _root catch-all, mapping keyed by folder ID; single collection + payload filter is the recorded lighter fallback if base folders proliferate; accepted: global search = client-side fan-out, base-folder delete = collection drop.
nodes.norm_label: d12: one collection per base folder

nodes.label: D13: Catalog Collection
nodes.rationale: Static config drifts from reality and no catalog forces consumers to guess; descriptions draw on names, paths and brief content excerpts (user choice: rich catalog).

nodes.label: D14: Hybrid From Day One
nodes.rationale: Supersedes the earlier dense-only-v1 lean — exact-token recall matters from day one (user 2026-07-26); learned sparse rejected for now because no serving path exposes bge-m3 lexical weights; future second slot via createVectorName.

nodes.label: Risk Register
nodes.rationale: Top risks: refresh-token revocation (loud AUTH_REQUIRED state), OCR cost surprise (counters make volume visible before invoices), DeepInfra dependency (swappable endpoint), sparse-encoder drift (shared module + golden vectors), sensitive payload text on a shared host (loopback-only Qdrant).

nodes.label: Open Questions Q1-Q6 (All Answered)
nodes.rationale: All answered 2026-07-26: Q1 work/school OneDrive (owned folder, plain Files.Read); Q2 bge-m3 via DeepInfra; Q3 Qwen3-VL OCR; Q4 corpus mostly digital PDFs; Q5 Docker on WSL2 now, VPS later; Q6 consumer is the owner's Node/TS app importing bm25-v1 directly.

nodes.label: Model and Provider Flexibility Feature Guide
nodes.norm_label: model and provider flexibility feature guide

nodes.label: Searching From Your App Feature Guide
nodes.norm_label: searching from your app feature guide

nodes.label: od_catalog Collection Registry
nodes.rationale: Dense-only by design: routing is semantic while hybrid search happens in document collections. Serves two first-class operations - enumerate (plain scroll, no LLM) and route (semantic query over the embedded name+description). Descriptions regenerate only on material content churn (over 20 percent) to bound LLM cost; updated_at exposes staleness.

nodes.label: conversationId
nodes.rationale: One conversationId names a whole thread, both sides; the app holds only this reference, never turn-level IDs.

nodes.label: app_conversations Collection
nodes.rationale: Owned by the consumer app and outside the managed od_* namespace so nothing vector-syncer does - sync, reconcile, rebuild, base-folder delete - can touch conversations; they survive OneDrive reorganizations and index rebuilds.

nodes.label: appendTurn
nodes.rationale: One small upsert per turn - the rest of the thread is never re-embedded; deterministic uuidv5 point IDs (conv:{conversationId}#{turnIndex}) make retries and edits overwrite instead of duplicate.

nodes.label: Shared Consumer Package (@vector-syncer/consumer)
nodes.rationale: Ships the bm25-v1 encoder and conversation helpers so the consumer app imports the exact modules the indexer uses instead of reimplementing them - prevents tokenizer and encoder drift. Ships in Phase 4.

nodes.label: OpenAI-Compatible Provider Contract
nodes.rationale: The system speaks exactly one API shape through the official OpenAI SDK; DeepInfra is a value, not a dependency - pointing OPENAI_BASE_URL at another provider moves worker and consumer app together. Five env vars are the whole contract; kill switches: empty OCR_LLM_MODEL disables vision, SPARSE_MODE=off forces dense-only writes.

nodes.label: Embedding Model Rebuild Cost
nodes.rationale: Embedding dimensions and semantics are baked into every collection, so changing EMBEDDING_MODEL is a re-index (zero-downtime _v2 build plus alias flip) while every other model or provider swap is a free config flip; finalize the embedding model before the first big backfill. Guarded: every point records embed_model and sparse_encoder, and the worker refuses to start against a mismatched vector size.

nodes.label: Graph Delta Query Polling
nodes.rationale: Cron-polled delta (default every 5 minutes via SYNC_CRON) processes only changed items so quiet polls are nearly free; webhooks deferred. On a sleeping machine syncs are delayed, never lost.

nodes.label: Base Folder to Collection Mapping (od_slug)
nodes.rationale: Each top-level subfolder gets its own collection od_{slug}, with od__root as catch-all. Mapping is keyed by folder ID, not name, so renaming a base folder never renames or rebuilds its collection; the catalog carries the current display name.

nodes.label: Weekly Reconcile
nodes.rationale: Re-checks everything end-to-end as the correctness backstop for any delta edge case missed live.

nodes.label: OneDrive as Single Source of Truth
nodes.rationale: Qdrant is a derived, rebuildable index; deletion in OneDrive always means deletion in Qdrant, and worst-case recovery from any data loss is one full resync - which is why Qdrant snapshots and Redis AOF backups are optional conveniences.
nodes.norm_label: onedrive as single source of truth

nodes.label: /health Endpoint
nodes.rationale: Wire to an uptime monitor on day one because the worst failure mode - a dead refresh token - is otherwise silent. Alert on auth not valid, stale lastSyncAt, climbing failed jobs, jumping ocr_images_processed (cost signal), climbing empty_conversion (unreadable documents).

nodes.label: Manual Sync Trigger
nodes.rationale: Always safe: the sync queue runs at concurrency 1 as a correctness invariant (deliberately not a knob), so a manual trigger queues behind any running walk and runs never overlap.

nodes.label: Live Files-Worker Concurrency
nodes.rationale: Runtime setting with no restart; baseline from FILE_CONCURRENCY, live overrides last until restart.

nodes.label: Resync and Rebuild Commands
nodes.rationale: Plain resync is cheap because hash-skip avoids re-embedding; resync --rebuild builds a _v2 collection and flips the alias for zero-downtime embedding-model, chunking, or OCR redo; resync --catalog refreshes catalog stats and descriptions on demand.

nodes.label: AUTH_REQUIRED Health State
nodes.rationale: Auth death halts loudly instead of crash-looping; recovery is a roughly 2-minute device-code re-login with all state intact and queued work resuming immediately.

nodes.label: Search Result Payload Contract
nodes.rationale: Every point carries everything needed to render a result - text, heading_path breadcrumb, file identity, web_url click-through, attribution - so no second lookup is ever required. Indexed filters: file_id, extension, mime_type, ancestor_ids, last_modified_ts.

nodes.label: Catalog-First Routing
nodes.rationale: Qdrant has no server-side cross-collection query, so ask the catalog which 1-3 collections fit the query, search those, and merge client-side; full fan-out over all collections stays acceptable only because the catalog keeps it rare.

nodes.label: Sparse-Only Degraded Mode
nodes.rationale: Dense query embedding needs the AI provider but sparse encoding is computed locally, so falling back to sparse-only keeps keyword search working through a provider outage.

nodes.label: Hybrid Search (Dense + Sparse RRF)
nodes.rationale: Hybrid from day one (D14): every point carries dense plus sparse vectors and queries prefetch both then fuse with RRF, so semantic paraphrases and exact tokens (invoice numbers, codes, names) both hit.

nodes.label: bm25-v1 Sparse Encoder
nodes.rationale: Unicode tokenize, lowercase, FNV-1a u32, BM25 TF saturation (k1=1.2 b=0.75 avgLen=256) with IDF applied server-side by Qdrant. Ships as an importable module and records sparse_encoder per point so indexer-vs-app drift is detectable; an encoder version bump is a sparse-only backfill with no re-embedding.

nodes.label: Hybrid Node + Python Runtime
nodes.rationale: BullMQ is Node-first and MarkItDown is Python-only, so the orchestrator is a Node/TypeScript worker with a Python FastAPI conversion sidecar (D1/D3).

nodes.label: Delegated Device-Code Auth
nodes.rationale: One-time device-code bootstrap into an encrypted persistent MSAL cache with silent refresh thereafter; failure becomes an AUTH_REQUIRED health state rather than a crash loop (D2). Work/school OneDrive owned by the signing-in user, so scopes are Files.Read offline_access User.Read against /me/drive.

nodes.label: BullMQ Queues (sync + files)
nodes.rationale: sync queue at concurrency 1 is a correctness invariant; files queue defaults to 4 and is live-adjustable at runtime; at-least-once delivery with dedup IDs and idempotent writes (D6).

nodes.label: MarkItDown Conversion Sidecar
nodes.rationale: One endpoint POST /convert; OCR on by default, inline, with no budget machinery because the corpus is mostly digital PDFs with minimal images; near-empty conversions warn and count instead of blocking (D8, simplified per owner).

nodes.label: Idempotent Writes (UUIDv5 Point IDs)
nodes.rationale: Point IDs are UUIDv5 of driveId/itemId#chunkIndex, job dedup IDs are itemId:cTag, and the delta token advances only after enqueue - any crash or retry re-produces identical writes; per-file updates are delete-then-upsert (D7).

nodes.label: One Collection per Base Folder
nodes.rationale: od_{slug} aliases over versioned physical collections, mapped by folder ID (rename-safe), with od__root as catch-all (D12); aliases make model or chunking changes a build-into-_v2-then-flip operation with zero downtime.

nodes.label: BAAI/bge-m3 Embedding Model
nodes.rationale: 1024-d dense embeddings (D4); the one expensive commitment since a change means re-indexing - finalize before the first big backfill. Documented self-host switch-back is a FlagEmbedding sidecar.

nodes.label: Change Classification
nodes.rationale: Delta items map to typed actions: new or changed content to process-file; rename or move within a base folder to update-metadata (payload patch only, no re-embedding); move across base folders to re-route (index new, purge old); file delete, folder delete (one ancestor_ids filter), and base-folder delete drops the whole collection plus catalog entry.

nodes.label: AES-256-GCM Cache Codec
nodes.rationale: Blob layout iv(12) | authTag(16) | ciphertext; random IV per call; throws on tamper or wrong key.

nodes.label: encryptedCachePlugin
nodes.rationale: Corrupt or unreadable cache warns and starts empty instead of throwing - the empty cache naturally forces the AuthRequiredError path later; cache file written mode 0600.

nodes.label: getGraphToken
nodes.rationale: Typed against a structural TokenApp subset of PublicClientApplication so token acquisition is testable without mocking the msal module; maps InteractionRequiredAuthError to AuthRequiredError and lets unexpected errors escape unchanged.

nodes.label: graphGet Client Wrapper
nodes.rationale: SDK client factory plus typed error mapping: 429 to RateLimitedError with retry-after ms, 410 to DeltaGoneError, everything else passes through.

nodes.label: DeltaGoneError
nodes.rationale: 410 Gone on delta means the token expired - restart enumeration with a fresh folder delta URL, never crash-loop.

nodes.label: resolveRoot
nodes.rationale: Resolves ONEDRIVE_FOLDER_PATH to driveId+folderId via Graph path addressing; the injected-get-function seam is the test strategy for everything Graph-facing.

nodes.label: walkDelta
nodes.rationale: Follows @odata.nextLink pages, invokes onPage per page, returns the final @odata.deltaLink; errors including DeltaGoneError propagate to the caller which owns restart policy.

nodes.label: classifyPage
nodes.rationale: Pure classifier from delta items to typed actions; folders are upserted before files within a page because delta pages can interleave; base folder resolution walks the parent chain with cycle guard and a fetchItem fallback; unresolvable ancestry is counted and skipped, never crashing.

nodes.label: devDelta CLI (yarn dev:delta)
nodes.rationale: The P1 deliverable: classified change listing with persistent deltaLink and 410 restart; P2's sync job reuses exactly this walk-classify-act composition, swapping print for enqueue.

nodes.label: Converter /healthz Endpoint
nodes.rationale: FastAPI skeleton reporting ocr_tier (none, llm, or docintel) from env; POST /convert arrives in the P3 plan on this same app.

nodes.label: Docker Compose Stack
nodes.rationale: Redis with noeviction and AOF (BullMQ requirement set now), Qdrant loopback-only, converter with healthcheck, worker; all ports loopback-only; service DNS names redis, qdrant, converter are what later plans' env defaults point at.

nodes.label: Phase-1 Delta Spike
nodes.rationale: Move-out-of-scope and folder-rename delta behavior are assumptions until verified on the real tenant; findings are written into the Graph integration doc and pinned as classifier regression tests, and the P2 plan is written only after this lands.
